extracted.intended_audience: general audience and people who want to improve their public speaking / vocal communication (presenters, speakers, professionals)
extracted.subtask_short: how to speak so people listen
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on vocal technique and interpersonal approach to make spoken communication more compelling so listeners pay attention. Covers vocal exercises and tips for speaking with empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make people want to listen
rubrics_metrics.description: How to speak so that people want to listen; addressing the common experience of talking but nobody listening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as the primary goal of the talk — improving how you speak so listeners engage. The page poses the problem ('Have you ever felt like you're talking, but nobody is listening?') and presents the talk as a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful speaking (the how-to's)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates the how-to's of powerful speaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as practical, actionable instruction in the talk; the page indicates the content includes concrete techniques rather than only theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of vocal exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: From some handy vocal exercises — the talk includes exercises to improve the voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocal exercises are cited as part of the toolkit for improving speaking (no specific exercises are listed on the page itself).

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak with empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tips on how to speak with empathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes empathetic speaking as a method to connect with listeners and make speech more effective; presented as a distinct element alongside vocal technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic goal: make the world sound more beautiful
rubrics_metrics.description: A talk that might help the world sound more beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers an aspirational/qualitative criterion: beyond technical effectiveness, speaking can aim for aesthetic improvement of sound and listening experience.
